extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on F1000Research’s open, post-publication peer review process including reviewer selection, report formats, approval statuses, and how to revise and respond to reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model — identity transparency (NISO terminology)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F1000Research uses the NISO standard terminology: reviewers’ identities and review information are published alongside the article. Reviewer interacts with: Editor, other reviewers, authors. Review information published: Review reports, submitted manuscript, reviewer identities. Post publication commenting: Open. This model supports transparent discussion of strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-led reviewer selection — minimum suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are responsible for identifying appropriate experts and must suggest at least 5 reviewers who meet our reviewer criteria before an article can be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guide to finding reviewers and the reviewer criteria is available on the Finding Article Reviewers page. The editorial team may also suggest suitable reviewers where required to ensure balance and facilitate peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer criteria must be met
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested reviewers must meet F1000Research’s reviewer criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team ensures the reviewer criteria are met. Authors should consult the Finding Article Reviewers page for the detailed criteria and guidance on suitable reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical expertise requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the study includes complex statistical analysis or new statistical methods, at least one of the initial reviewer suggestions should have a proven track record as a statistics expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may request additional statistics experts as the peer review process progresses, so authors should be prepared to suggest more if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not approach reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should not approach reviewers about the peer review process independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting reviewers directly has the potential to influence and invalidate their review; the editorial team acts as the intermediary and contacts reviewers on behalf of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial team responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The editorial team supports authors during peer review and performs several tasks to manage the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific tasks include: ensuring reviewer criteria are met; acting as intermediary between authors and reviewers; contacting reviewers; ensuring all aspects of an article are reviewed; checking peer review reports before they are published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of peer review reports with reviewer names and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review reports are published alongside the article with the names and affiliations of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing reports and reviewer identities enables transparent discussion of the article’s strengths and weaknesses. Each peer review report also contains answers to reviewer questions tailored to each article type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer reports must answer tailored reviewer questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer review report contains answers to the reviewer questions tailored to the article type published on F1000Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tailored questions guide reviewers to comment on relevant aspects of the manuscript according to article type (see Reviewer Guidelines for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved: No or only minor changes are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original research this means the aims and research methods are adequate; results are presented accurately; and the conclusions are justified and supported by the presented data or supporting material. Reviewers may suggest small changes to improve the article or correct minor errors, but these changes will not affect the peer review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Approved with Reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved with Reservations: The reviewer believes the article has academic merit but has asked for a number of small changes to the article, or specific, sometimes more significant revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should make clear that the changes requested are necessary for an Approved status to be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status: Not Approved
rubrics_metrics.description: Not Approved: The article in its current form has issues that seriously undermine the findings and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial substantial revisions will be required for the paper to pass peer review. Not Approved is not a rejection; authors can improve an article’s status from Not Approved to Approved upon publication of a new version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiently reviewed threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: An article is considered to have been sufficiently reviewed when it has received two peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an article has not passed peer review at this stage, authors will be strongly encouraged to revise their paper and respond to reviewers by publishing a new version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passing peer review — numeric thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: An article is considered to have passed peer review when at least two ‘Approved’ statuses, or one ‘Approved’ and two ‘Approved with Reservations’ have been awarded by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some articles may have more than two peer review reports (e.g., additional reviewers accepted invitations or special expertise was required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising and responding to reviewers — point-by-point response
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide a direct point-by-point response to each reviewer when they submit the revised article version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response should explain how each of the reviewers’ comments have been addressed in the revisions. This helps original reviewers re-assess the work and signals to potential reviewers that feedback is being taken into consideration, increasing the likelihood that further reviewers will agree to review the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-invitation of original reviewers and status updates
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new version is published, the original reviewers are re-invited to review and may publish an updated report taking the revisions into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are especially encouraged to re-review if they had originally given an ‘Approved with Reservations’ or ‘Not Approved’ status, so they can assess whether the work has been sufficiently improved to achieve a better approval status. Reviewers may update the peer review status awarded to an article; if unresolved issues remain, authors will be encouraged to revise again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent publication of versions and review history
rubrics_metrics.description: All versions of the article, and all peer review reports, remain published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the full history of the article and peer review, allowing anyone to see changes over time and the reviewers’ reports for each version.
